micro_interview.question: You benchmark the same numerical kernel in Python and C++. C++ is 20x faster on one dataset but only 2x faster on another. Before claiming C++ is intrinsically better, what would you investigate?
micro_interview.demonstrate: Experimental discipline: algorithmic equivalence, vectorized/library backends, input size, cache/memory effects, interpreter overhead, compiler optimisation, warm-up, I/O and reproducibility.
micro_interview.practice: Take 6 minutes to list hypotheses and one discriminating experiment for each. Then give a 3-minute English answer beginning with measurement validity rather than language preference; do not solve every branch.

life_career_actions.suggestion: Close the CERN 215 decision today and, if the evidence is defensible, submit well before the 23:59 CEST deadline; otherwise record DISCARD and move directly to Optiver London or Barclays Quant.
Spend 45 minutes turning one TFM result into a reproducible English GitHub mini-case with problem, method, experiment, result and limitations.
Consider a 30–45 minute sport or movement block and one screen-free break after the deadline-critical application work, before returning to portfolio or interview practice.
